integrated_description: Adopt a rescue animal—prioritizing adult and senior animals alongside younger ones—through rigorous pre-adoption screening (behavioral assessment, health evaluation, lifestyle and housing matching, veterinary budget and contingency planning) combined with post-adoption surrender-risk reduction commitments including a defined transition support window, access to training resources, and scheduled rescue follow-up; adoption remains the clear default, with a documented good-faith search required before considering a reputable breeder as a last resort only in rare circumstances where adoption genuinely cannot meet specific welfare or functional needs (e.g., certified service animal roles), and only from breeders meeting strict standards of health testing, full transparency, welfare-centered limited production, buyer-return clauses, and no broker sales. Systemic commitment must include at least one tangible, ongoing channel—such as shelter volunteering, fostering, financial support for rescue operations, low-cost spay/neuter promotion, or local post-adoption outreach—focused on supporting responsible pet retention, reducing returns, and expanding community access to education and training resources rather than enforcing a simplistic adopt-vs-buy binary.
integration_rationale: All three stakeholders accepted the core synthesis and requested compatible elaborations—clearer decision rules and fallback criteria, operational post-adoption commitments, and advocacy reframing—which were layered into a single coherent proposal without contradicting the original adoption-first, systemic-commitment direction. Where modifications overlapped (surrender-risk reduction, breeder exception criteria, advocacy specificity), they were merged into unified language that satisfies each stakeholder's intent simultaneously.
